examples.en: We are on such close terms that we talk without reserve.

examples.ko: 선배가 격의 없는 태도로 저를 대해 줬어요.
examples.en: My senior treated me in a friendly, unreserved way.

examples.ko: 서로 격의 없어서 같이 있으면 편해요.
examples.en: We're so open with each other that it's comfortable to be together.

examples.ko: 앞으로는 격의 없게 지내자고 먼저 말했어요.
examples.en: I was the first to say that we should be casual with each other from now on.

examples.ko: 우리 사이에 격의 없다고 생각해서 솔직히 말했어요.
examples.en: I thought we had no need for formality between us, so I spoke honestly.
We're comfortable with each other now, so please speak freely.

explain: 거의 '격의 없다/없이'의 모양으로만 써요. 사이가 가까워서 어려워하거나 예의를 너무 차리지 않아도 되는 관계에 쓰고, 좋은 뜻이에요. '격의 없이 지내다/대하다/말하다'가 자주 쓰여요.

phrases.example: 저희는 격의 없는 사이라서 뭐든 말해요.
phrases.en: We're so close that we can say anything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 예의를 너무 차리지 않아도 되는 가까운 관계를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a close relationship without stiff formality.

phrases.en: Please feel free to speak openly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려워하지 말고 편하게 말하라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone to speak without holding back.

phrases.en: I get along with my neighbors without any formality.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to 격의 없이.

explain_en: It is used almost only in the form '격의 없다/없이'. It describes a close relationship where you don't have to be shy or overly formal, and it has a positive meaning. Common patterns are '격의 없이 지내다/대하다/말하다'.

examples.en: The adoptee grew up and found his birth mother.

examples.ko: 그의 생모는 어릴 때 집을 떠났대요.
examples.en: I heard his birth mother left home when he was young.

examples.ko: 생모와 양모를 함께 만나는 자리가 마련됐어요.
examples.en: A meeting was arranged with both the birth mother and the adoptive mother.
The court accepted the birth mother's request.
I received a letter from my birth mother and cried for a long time.
I didn't know who my birth mother was, but I grew up loved.

explain: 자기를 낳아 준 어머니를 가리키는데, 입양이나 재혼, 법적인 설명처럼 '낳은 어머니'를 구별해야 할 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '친어머니'라고도 해요. 평소에 어머니를 부를 때는 '엄마', '어머니'를 쓰고 '생모'라고 부르지 않아요.

phrases.example: 저는 친어머니를 한 번도 본 적이 없어요.
phrases.en: I have never met my birth mother.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but sounds less formal than '생모'.

phrases.en: He met his birth mother after he grew up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낳아 준 어머니를 만나는 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in stories about meeting the mother who gave birth to you.

phrases.en: I know neither my birth mother nor my birth father.
phrases.nuance_en: '생부' means birth father and pairs with '생모'.

explain_en: It refers to the mother who gave birth to you and is used when you need to distinguish the birth mother, such as in adoption, remarriage or legal explanations. '친어머니' means the same. In everyday life you call your mother '엄마' or '어머니', never '생모'.

en: to attend; to serve; to look after

examples.en: The granddaughter waits on her grandmother at her side.
In the old days, servants waited on their masters.

examples.ko: 아픈 남편을 시중드느라 쉴 틈이 없었어요.
examples.en: I had no time to rest because I was taking care of my sick husband.

examples.ko: 시중들 사람이 없어서 제가 직접 했어요.
examples.en: There was no one to attend to things, so I did it myself.

examples.ko: 그는 하루 종일 손님을 시중드는 일을 해요.
examples.en: His job is attending to guests all day.
My stamina dropped a lot while I was looking after the patient.

explain: 옆에서 식사나 몸 씻기 같은 자잘한 일을 돌봐 주는 것을 말해요. ㄹ이 있는 동사라서 '시중드는', '시중드세요'처럼 ㄹ이 빠지는 활용에 주의하세요. '시중을 들다'로 띄어 써도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The nurse attends to the patient.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시중들다'를 띄어 쓴 꼴로, '~의 시중을 들다'처럼 대상을 앞에 넣어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced form of 시중들다; the person is put in front, as in '~의 시중을 들다'.

phrases.example: 할머니 곁에는 시중드는 사람이 따로 있어요.
phrases.en: Grandmother has a separate person who attends to her.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㄹ이 빠지는 활용이에요. 돌봐 주는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ㄹ drops in this conjugation; refers to a person who looks after someone.

phrases.example: 어머니는 아픈 아버지를 오래 시중들어 주셨어요.
phrases.en: My mother looked after my sick father for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-어 주다'를 붙여 상대를 위해 돌봐 준다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -어 주다 adds the sense of attending to someone for their sake.

explain_en: It means staying beside someone and taking care of small needs such as meals and personal care. The final ㄹ drops in some forms, as in '시중드는' and '시중드세요', so watch the conjugation. You also often see it written as '시중을 들다'.

examples.en: My wife's brother is getting married this weekend.

examples.ko: 저는 처남과 같이 낚시를 자주 가요.
examples.en: I often go fishing with my wife's brother.

examples.ko: 처남이 새 차를 사서 구경하러 갔어요.
examples.en: My brother-in-law bought a new car, so I went to see it.
My wife's younger brother is my brother-in-law.
Thanks to my brother-in-law, I was introduced to a good job.

examples.ko: 명절에 처남 가족이 우리 집에 와요.
examples.en: My brother-in-law's family comes to our house for the holiday.

explain: '처남'은 아내의 남자 형제를 부르거나 가리키는 말이에요. 아내의 여자 형제는 '처형'(언니)과 '처제'(동생)라고 해요. 남편의 남자 형제는 '시숙', '도련님' 등 따로 있어서 영어의 brother-in-law보다 훨씬 세분돼 있어요.

phrases.en: My brother-in-law's wife sent me some tasty side dishes.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the wife of one's wife's brother.

phrases.en: I watched soccer with my brother-in-law on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_en: More casual than 과/와, common in conversation.

phrases.en: I called my brother-in-law and asked how he was.
phrases.nuance_en: A particle that sounds more natural in speech than 에게.

explain_en: 처남 is the wife's brother. The wife's sisters are 처형 (older) and 처제 (younger). Korean splits in-laws much more finely than English: the husband's brothers have their own terms such as 도련님.

examples.en: My wife's younger sister lives near our house.
I sent a birthday present to my wife's younger sister.
I went to see a movie with my wife's younger sister.
My wife's younger sister is getting married next month.
My wife's younger sister and her husband came to visit on the weekend.
I tend to call my wife's younger sister by her name.

explain: 남편이 아내의 여동생을 말할 때 써요. 아내의 언니는 '처형'이라고 해요. 직접 부를 때도 '처제'라고 부르거나 이름을 불러요.

phrases.example: 주말에 처제네 집에 가서 저녁을 먹었어요.
phrases.en: On the weekend, we went to my sister-in-law's house and had dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-네'를 붙여 그 사람의 집이나 가족을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -네 refers to that person's home or family.

phrases.en: My sister-in-law and her husband had a baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처제와 그 남편을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to refer to your sister-in-law and her husband together.

phrases.example: 처형과 처제가 같이 우리 집에 왔어요.
phrases.en: My wife's older sister and younger sister came to our house together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처형은 아내의 언니이고, 처제는 아내의 여동생이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 처형 is the wife's older sister, while 처제 is her younger sister.

explain_en: A husband uses it for his wife's younger sister. His wife's older sister is '처형'. You can also address her directly as '처제' or by name.

en: to be close; to be intimate

examples.ko: 우리 반 친구들은 서로 아주 친밀해요.
examples.en: The friends in my class are very close to each other.

examples.ko: 친밀한 사이일수록 예의를 지키는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: The closer the relationship, the more important manners are.

examples.ko: 그 두 사람은 오랫동안 친밀하게 지냈어요.
examples.en: Those two have been close for a long time.

examples.ko: 회사 사람들과 친밀해지려고 같이 점심을 먹어요.
examples.en: I eat lunch with coworkers to get closer to them.

examples.ko: 친밀하지 않은 사람에게는 반말을 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't use casual speech with people you aren't close to.
I want to build a close relationship with my child.

explain: '친하다'보다 딱딱하고 글에 어울려요. '친하다'는 사람 사이를 편하게 말하고, '친밀하다'는 관계가 가까운 정도를 설명하는 말이에요. 그래서 '친구와 친밀하다'보다 '친구와 친하다'가 입말에서 훨씬 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The two of them are very close.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 명사 앞에서 꾸며 줄 때 써요. '친한 사이'보다 조금 딱딱해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun; a bit stiffer than 친한 사이.

phrases.en: We became closer through traveling together.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a relationship gradually gets closer.

phrases.en: I am very close with that friend.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, 친하다 is much more natural than 친밀하다.

explain_en: More formal and bookish than '친하다'. '친하다' is how you casually describe being friends; '친밀하다' describes the degree of closeness in a relationship. In speech '친구와 친하다' is much more natural than '친구와 친밀하다'.
